findings.title: Titles shaped like `task-N` are now rejected although ids already take precedence in lookup
findings.why: `find` in list.ts tries `tasks.get(key)` (the id) before `byTitle`, so an id never resolves to a task by title. The new rule therefore adds no safety. It makes `add`, `rename` and `importTasks` reject valid titles such as 'task-5', which the task-003 spec does not allow. Imported lines with such titles are rejected with a confusing message. A task titled 'task-2' could not be reached by its title while a task with id 'task-2' exists. That is a lookup-ambiguity matter, and rejecting the title does not address it.

findings.title: The id format is duplicated as a regex, away from where ids are generated
findings.why: Ids are produced by `task-${++issued}` in list.ts:88, while this regex in task.ts hard-codes the same format. If the id scheme changes, the guard will quietly stop matching, and nothing ties the two together.

findings.title: The validation spec does not list the new title rule
findings.why: task-003 lists the rejected inputs (empty title, over 120 characters, bad priority, bad tag). The new 'looks like a task id' rejection is documented only in the code comment and the test, so the project's documentation contradicts the behaviour.
